source: Rasch and Born (2013) About sleep's role in memory
finding: Review states the active systems model: in slow-wave sleep, slow oscillations drive hippocampal ripples nested in thalamo-cortical spindles; this redistributes memory to cortex. Contrasts it with passive accounts where sleep only cuts interference.
numbers: Spindle-ripple events nested in slow-oscillation up phases; REM assumed to stabilise synaptically afterwards.
quote: memory consolidation during sleep is selective
limits: Model is a synthesis; the review itself flags that what decides which memories get consolidated is poorly understood.
agent_relevance: The core claim for our agent: consolidation is an active, selective offline job, not just rest. The selection rule is the open design question.

source: Rasch and Born (2013) - gist, inference, insight evidence
finding: Behavioural evidence for qualitative reorganisation: sleep helps gist, hidden-rule insight (number reduction task), transitive inference (A>E after learning A>B etc.), explicit sequence knowledge from implicit SRTT training, statistical learning, and more DRM false recall.
numbers: Review text: wake controls stayed at chance on the explicit SRTT generation task; DRM sleep effect less consistent with recognition than free recall.
limits: Many of these effects are inconsistent across labs; DRM and lexical-integration effects carry 'but see' citations in the same review.
agent_relevance: Supports 'episodes into rules' as the benefit of offline work, but each claim needs its own test; none is guaranteed.

source: Rasch and Born (2013) - selectivity and non-replicated skill gains
finding: Review concedes that procedural gains attributed to sleep can appear within hours of wake (a recovery effect), and some studies find no sleep-dependent motor gain once circadian and homeostatic factors are controlled.
numbers: Cites refs 164, 991, 995 for null sleep gains in motor tasks.
limits: Counter-evidence is reported by authors who support the theory.
agent_relevance: Part of the benefit may be rest or time, not replay. Our agent needs a time-matched no-consolidation control.

source: Hu et al. (2020) Promoting memory consolidation during sleep: meta-analysis of targeted memory reactivation
finding: First TMR meta-analysis: cueing in sleep helps memory. The effect works in NREM, not in REM or wake.
numbers: 91 experiments, 212 effect sizes, N=2004. Overall g=0.29 [0.21,0.38]; NREM2 g=0.32 [0.04,0.60]; SWS g=0.27 [0.20,0.35]; REM and wake not significant. Heterogeneity Q(211)=588, I2=71%.
limits: Small effect; high heterogeneity.
agent_relevance: Causal support for reactivation as the active ingredient. The effect is small, so expect modest gains from a reactivation job.

source: Hu et al. (2020) - publication bias analysis
finding: Funnel plot was asymmetric (Egger Z=8.489, p<.001); the effect shrinks after correction but stays above zero.
numbers: Trim-and-fill adjusted g=0.18 [0.06,0.30]. Unpublished studies (k=26) g=0.18 [-0.06,0.42], ns; published (k=186) g=0.31.
limits: Adjusted effect is about 40% smaller than the headline.
agent_relevance: Discount headline sleep effects by roughly 40% when budgeting expected benefit.

source: Hu et al. (2020) - domain moderators
finding: TMR effect differs by task: associative learning gains were small; skill tasks also benefited overall. The founding Rasch 2007 finger-tapping skill condition was null in the coded data.
numbers: Associative learning in NREM g=0.17 [0.03,0.30], p=.019. Rasch 2007 Exp1 skill g=-0.08 [-0.52,0.37]; spatial declarative g=0.69 [0.19,1.18].
limits: Founding study had very small per-condition samples (about 7 to 17 as coded).
agent_relevance: Reactivation helps hippocampus-linked declarative material most; do not assume it helps every skill.

source: Ng, Noh and Spencer (2025) Bayesian meta-analysis of slow oscillation-spindle coupling and memory
finding: Active-systems mechanism check: precise slow-oscillation/spindle coupling relates to memory retention, but the link is small.
numbers: 23 studies, 297 effect sizes (17 overnight, 6 nap). Pooled phase-memory r=0.07 [0.01,0.13], BF10=58.35, posterior probability 0.98.
limits: Small r; heterogeneity; moderated by memory type, age, spindle frequency, cortical site. Correlational.
agent_relevance: Mechanism is supported but weak: the dialogue explains little variance alone. Do not over-credit one mechanism.

source: Ng et al. (2025) - moderators
finding: Coupling-memory link is weaker with age and strongest for frontal fast spindles; memory type mattered (6 procedural vs 19 declarative tasks).
numbers: Age slope remained after removing older adults: -0.005 [-0.015,0.008], BF10=4.05. Fast (k=41) vs slow (k=26) spindle difference r=-0.02, BF10=1.91, inconclusive.
limits: Several moderator tests give only anecdotal-to-moderate Bayes factors.
agent_relevance: Boundary conditions matter: the effect depends on who and what is consolidated; test per task type.

source: Ng et al. (2025) - risk of bias
finding: ROBINS-I risk of bias was moderate overall after requesting unreported data; outcome measurement was the most heterogeneous domain.
numbers: 23 studies; 297 effect sizes after data transformation.
limits: Correlational designs, not causal.
agent_relevance: Correlational mechanism evidence is the weakest link; causal evidence comes from TMR and stimulation.

source: Ngo and Staresina (2022) Slow-oscillation closed-loop TMR
finding: Cues timed to slow-oscillation UP states cut overnight forgetting more than cues at DOWN states. Timing of replay matters, not only replay.
numbers: N=24 (2 excluded). Forgetting 5% (UP) vs 15% (DOWN), t(23)=2.28, p=.032; uncued 12%, not different from either (p>.67). UP cueing also gave greater spindle power and reinstated image representations.
limits: Small N; UP and uncued did not differ significantly; one lab.
agent_relevance: Offline replay should be gated by a good moment or state, not run blindly; gains are small and need replication.

source: Hu et al. (2020) - mechanism: auditory cues reach cortex
finding: Narrative section: auditory TMR works despite thalamic gating, and it can boost a chosen subset of memories from one learning episode.
numbers: Describes Rasch 2007 and later object-sound studies.
limits: Narrative only.
agent_relevance: Item-level selectivity is possible: choose which episodes to replay.

source: Marshall, Helgadottir, Molle and Born (2006) Boosting slow oscillations during sleep potentiates memory
finding: Founding causal test: 0.75 Hz oscillating current in early NREM sleep boosted slow oscillations and retention of hippocampus-dependent declarative memory; 5 Hz did not.
numbers: Abstract: increased SWS, slow oscillations and slow spindle activity; 5 Hz decreased slow oscillations with no memory change. Exact figures not read.
limits: Abstract only; later tES replications mixed (see Cordi and Rasch 2021).
agent_relevance: Mechanism is causal, not only correlated; not directly transferable.

source: Rasch, Buchel, Gais and Born (2007) Odor cues during slow-wave sleep prompt declarative memory consolidation
finding: Founding TMR study: odor present at learning and re-presented in SWS improved declarative recall; no effect in REM, wake, or if the odor was absent at learning.
numbers: fMRI showed hippocampal activation to odor in SWS. Per-condition samples small (about 7 to 17 per Hu 2020 coding).
limits: Abstract read only; small samples.
agent_relevance: Reactivation needs the cue linked at encoding. For an agent: tag episodes with retrieval keys at write time.

source: Cordi and Rasch (2021) How robust are sleep-mediated memory benefits?
finding: Review of replication failures: key sleep-memory findings could not be replicated or held only under conditions. Effects smaller, more task-dependent, less SWS-related and less lasting than assumed.
numbers: Abstract states claims qualitatively; no single effect size.
quote: effects of sleep on memory are smaller, more task-dependent, less SWS-related, less robust
limits: Abstract only; authors include a leading proponent.
agent_relevance: Strongest caution: treat the human evidence as modest and fragile when borrowing it as design justification.

source: Ball, Kimel, Keller, Ward, Cai et al. (2025) No evidence for a TMR effect on word-meaning priming
finding: A nap TMR test found no extra benefit of cueing on priming or contextual recall, even though cue-evoked spindle/beta power rose.
numbers: 80 homonyms, 40 primed, about 2 h nap, half of cues replayed plus 20 control cues; no TMR benefit; neural reprocessing signature present.
limits: Abstract only; one task type.
agent_relevance: Neural replay signature without behavioural gain: reactivation can happen and still not help. Measure outcome, not activity.

source: Lowe, Petzka, Tzegka and Schuck (2024) N2 sleep inspires insight
finding: Preregistered test of sleep and insight: N2 sleep, not N1, raised insight likelihood after a 20 min nap. Authors note earlier results conflicted.
numbers: N=90, perceptual insight task before and after a nap.
limits: Abstract only. Nap, not overnight.
agent_relevance: Rule discovery after offline time is real but stage-dependent and not reliable; do not assume any offline pass yields insight.

source: Lewis and Durrant (2011) Overlapping memory replay during sleep builds cognitive schemata (iOtA)
finding: Proposes that overlapping replay of related memories strengthens shared elements, and repeated replay in different combinations builds schemas, gist, insight and false memory.
numbers: Theoretical model; no effect sizes.
limits: Abstract only. Predicts false memories as a cost.
agent_relevance: Blueprint for episodes-to-rules: replay overlapping episodes together and keep what is shared. Cost: more false generalisation.

source: Lin, Snell, Stoica, Gonzalez et al. (2025) Sleep-time compute
finding: Offline precomputation over context before the query cuts test-time compute for the same accuracy and, scaled up, raises accuracy.
numbers: About 5x less test-time compute at equal accuracy on Stateful GSM-Symbolic and Stateful AIME; up to +13% (GSM) and +18% (AIME) accuracy with more sleep-time compute; 2.5x lower average cost per query with 10 related queries.
limits: Benchmarks built by the authors; gains depend on query predictability.
agent_relevance: Closest analogue to an offline job: precompute derived facts. Gains only where later queries are predictable from stored context.

source: Lin et al. (2025) - predictability moderator and pass@k
finding: Benefit tracks how predictable the question is from the context (log-probability under Llama2-70B). Sleep-time compute Pareto-dominates parallel pass@k at matched cost.
numbers: Section 5.4: predictable questions benefit more; Fig 6 pass@k vs sleep-time on Stateful AIME.
limits: Predictability is a proxy; values are in figures, not recorded here.
agent_relevance: Decide offline-work budget by how predictable future tasks are. Unpredictable tasks: skip it.

source: LightMem authors (2025) LightMem: lightweight memory-augmented generation (ICLR 2026)
finding: Memory system with an offline sleep-time update that reorganises, de-duplicates and abstracts entries; the online path only appends (soft update).
numbers: LongMemEval and LoCoMo, GPT and Qwen backbones: QA accuracy up to +7.7% / +29.3%; total tokens down up to 38x / 20.9x; API calls down up to 30x / 55.5x; online-only tokens down up to 106x / 117x.
limits: Gains come from the whole pipeline; the sleep-time step's own accuracy contribution was not isolated in what I read.
agent_relevance: Pattern: write cheap and lossless online, consolidate offline. Hard online overwrites lost information in their Tokyo/Kyoto example.

source: Han (2026) Memory depth, not memory access: selective parametric consolidation (EVAF)
finding: Surprise-times-valence gated LoRA writes keep goals after context unload; retrieval still wins on plain facts. Stale-memory invalidation stayed unresolved.
numbers: GPT-2 and TinyLlama: retrieval short-fact accuracy 0.956 to 0.973; EVAF goal persistence and post-unload recovery 0.812 to 0.904 with 2 to 3 parametric writes per 200 events. Matched random gates isolate selection.
limits: Synthetic streams, small models; Mistral-7B showed model-dependent write strength; single author.
agent_relevance: Selective consolidation (what to keep) matters; but weight training is outside our no-training scaffold. Reuse the gate idea for rule memory.

source: Dual-Layer Agentic Memory (2026) fast write routing and slow consolidation
finding: CLS-inspired agent memory: filter writes with a small-to-large cascade, then periodically consolidate high-value memories into weights.
numbers: 1.7B/8B cascade prunes up to 68% of redundant external memory, escalates under 50% of inputs, keeps over 98% of QA exact match of an exhaustive-retention baseline.
limits: Abstract read only; consolidation by fine-tuning.
agent_relevance: Pruning and consolidating memory can cut size with little accuracy loss.

source: Bazhenov, Delanois and Krishnan (2026) Sleep-inspired replay after sequential tasks
finding: Unsupervised sleep-like replay after five sequential tasks partially restores old-task accuracy; old-task information decays gradually with each new task.
numbers: MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10; tasks 1 to 5 trained before one sleep phase; accuracy falls with more tasks before sleep but is partly recovered. Exact figures only in plots.
limits: Small image benchmarks, not LLMs; recovery partial.
agent_relevance: Wait too long and traces fade. Run the offline job often enough.

source: CodaRAG (2026) Connecting the dots with associativity inspired by complementary learning
finding: Graph RAG that consolidates fragmented entities into one substrate before retrieval, then regulates interference.
numbers: Method text read; benchmark numbers not extracted.
limits: Headline results not recorded.
agent_relevance: Consolidation as entity merging is a cheap rule-extraction step, but unmeasured here.

source: Rasch and Born (2013) - synaptic stabilisation and sequential hypothesis
finding: Review notes that many findings fit the sequential hypothesis (SWS then REM) but it was rarely tested directly, and that sleep-cycle organisation, not just stage amounts, may drive effects.
numbers: No pooled numbers; text states the sequential hypothesis has rarely been subjected to direct testing.
limits: Rival to simple SWS-only account; unresolved in the review.
agent_relevance: If offline work has two phases (replay then stabilise), test the order; do not assume one pass is enough.
